newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Pliva says H1 EPS up to 520 from 457 kuna.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Pliva says H1 EPS up to 520 from 457 kuna.

text.p: Leading Croatian pharmaceutical firm Pliva d.d. said on Monday its per share earnings (EPS) had gone up to almost 520 kuna thanks to "extremely good results" for the first half this year, from 457 kuna a year ago.
"This is a significant rise, taking into account that (at the end of) June there were 60,000 more shares outstanding than in the year-ago period," chief executive Zeljko Covic told reporters.
Pliva's global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at 50 to each share, have soared to over $52 on the London Stock Exchange from $18.71 in March, when they were floated.
Earlier today, the company reported a 49.5 percent leap in January-June preliminary pre-tax profit to 368.3 million kuna from the first six months of 1995.
Its net income rose to 283.9 from 222.5 million kuna, or 27.6 percent, as total turnover increased 15.1 percent to 1.2 billion kuna and the company cut costs by two percent.
"The six-month results are extremely good," Covic said, adding that all of Pliva's businesses, including cosmetics, veterinary and agricultural products, recorded an output growth.
He said exports rose to $102 million from $86 million at the expense of domestic sales, whose share shrank to 34 from 37 percent of the total.
Among future goals Covic outlined strong investments into further development and expansion on larger foreign markets, particularly in central and eastern European countries.
He said the company was considering a number of investment projects in those countries, from sales and manufacturing of its products under license to joint ventures and mergers.

Pliva, the world's fifth largest manufacturer of Vitamin C, also has one world-class drug, an antibiotic marketed in western Europe and Americas as Zithromax under license from Pfizer Inc and as azithromycin in the rest of Europe. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
